A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairGen work. Their complete main text, Appendices A–E, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HBE and Stable Bias experiments, ablations, human validation of attribute detection, runtime measurements, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds SD-3.5-Large evaluations, Stable Bias age and race results, and additional generated-image examples.

M1.justification: The adaptive latent guidance, memory-based indicator, and SFT/DPO training of the prompt generator remain unchanged. Evaluating SD-3.5-Large introduces no documented modification to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Stable Bias occupation evaluation expands from gender alone to gender, age, and race in Table 7. HBE's domains, prompt coverage, and attribute tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 7 retain vanilla generation, prompt intervention, distribution-alignment finetuning, and FairDiffusion. The added model and attribute evaluations use this same comparator set; Table 8's LLM-prompting comparison is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Table 2 add SD-3.5-Large alongside SD2 and SDXL. Existing data splits, bias and CLIP metrics, and guidance-timing settings remain unchanged, making this a limited extension of evaluated model configurations.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds qualitative cases illustrating balanced gender generation with SD-3.5-Large. The target-proportion, diffusion-stage, SFT/DPO, and attribute-judge analyses are retained without new controlled ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report T=10 Monte Carlo samples. Table 3 retains its standard deviation across target proportions, rather than repeated runs. No seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added.

E6.justification: Substantial result blocks are added: Table 2 reports SD-3.5-Large comparisons across four attribute settings, with FairGen bias scores 0.118, 0.194, 0.381, and 0.397. Table 7 adds age and race comparisons, including FairGen scores 0.206 and 0.189. Existing table values remain unchanged; these are additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the bias-score definition, and Appendix B's diffusion formulation retain the same mathematical content. Notation spacing and wording changes introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adaptive inference-time attribute control, memory-based distribution tracking, HBE, and bias reduction while preserving generation quality. Additional evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a limitation concerning throughput-sensitive applications and the fairness–efficiency tradeoff. Section 5.1 removes the detailed cross-benchmark argument about prompt-complexity robustness, although related introductory claims remain. The expanded runtime explanation already appeared in v1 Appendix E.3.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page data-repository link and explicitly identifies SD2 in the captions of Table 3 and Figure 2. These improve access instructions and setting documentation; the training description and appendix prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 revises Stable Bias's described attribute coverage from gender/race to gender/race/age, refining the comparison with prior benchmarks. The additional Esser 2024b reference is a preprint entry for an already cited work, not a distinct literature addition.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion receive localized rewrites, wording and cross-references are edited, and Section 5.4 incorporates runtime explanation already present in the appendix. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a model block, Table 7 expands to three attribute groups and moves to a full-width position, and Figure 3 is added. Existing figures are retained with layout adjustments and caption edits. Table 2's caption still names only two models despite displaying three.

improvement.justification: The additional model and attribute comparisons in Tables 2 and 7 broaden empirical support, while the data-access link and throughput limitation improve transparency. These incremental gains outweigh the loss of the detailed prompt-complexity discussion and minor editing inconsistencies, including Table 2's outdated caption.
